To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the carbon stocks of dead wood in the coppice forests of Turkey are significantly different from each other, and the carbon stocks are significantly correlated with the diameter at breast height, age, basal areas, and the carbon stock of aboveground biomass.

carbon stocks of fine woody dead debris were determined to have significant correlation (p < 0.05, r > 0.70) with diameter at breast height, age, basal areas, and carbon stocks in aboveground biomass.
fine woody debris is the most important carbon stock component in coppice-origin forests and that carbon stocks of this component are affected by the development stage of the forest.
In summary, our research is concerned with
carbon stocks of dead wood in addition to carbon budgets of the whole ecosystem.
a new approach for carbon stock assessments and management strategies of coppice-originated forests.
the carbon stocks of dead wood in coppice-origin oak forests and the effects of forest management practices on these carbon stocks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
coppice forests have a high potential for carbon sequestration and storage, especially in fine woody debris.
coppice-originated forest management has a significant effect on carbon budgets.
coppice-originated forests have a significant potential to sequester carbon in FWD, and this should be taken into consideration for the future carbon budget of Turkey.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
carbon stocks of fine woody biomass in coppice forests are important in the carbon cycle and that these carbon stocks should be included in carbon budgets of forest ecosystems.
carbon stocks of fine woody residues in coppice oak forests are not negligible, and that the carbon budget should include the fine woody residues.
coppice forests should be managed in a way to keep the forest in coppice form, and the carbon stocks of fine woody materials should be taken into account for the carbon cycle of the forest ecosystem.
The main takeaway from our work is that
FWD is an important part of carbon stocks in the coppice oak forest ecosystem and that the management of coppice-originated forests is an effective tool for carbon budgeting in the forest ecosystem.
carbon budgets of coppice forests can be improved by increasing the age and diameter of trees, and by reducing the intensity of coppicing.
FWD is an important component of the carbon stocks of coppice forests, and it should be considered in the national carbon budgets.
